archetype.name: Fringe Contender (all offense)
archetype.definition: A top-three offense attached to a bottom-two defense, good enough to beat most teams in a shootout but too leaky to be trusted to separate from anyone.

report.headline: Elite Prescott passing game, a defense that can't get off the field
report.take:
Dallas is the same team it was in 2025, only with the offense pushed further up. Last year's Cowboys ranked 5th in offensive EPA and 32nd in defensive EPA. This year it is 2nd and 31st. The 2-2 record is honest. Wins over expected sit at -0.07 and turnover margin is dead even, so neither luck nor giveaways explain the record. A +2.5 point differential and a 13th-ranked net EPA describe a team that wins the games its offense can win and loses the ones its defense can't hold.

The engine is Prescott's passing game. Pass EPA ranks 3rd and success rate 4th, and he has turned it over only twice in four games. The line does real work: a 3.6% sack rate ranks 6th even though his time to throw ranks 25th, which means he holds the ball and stays clean. CeeDee Lamb's 46 targets, 11.5 a game, make the hierarchy obvious. George Pickens and Ryan Flournoy split the rest. The run game is the soft spot. It averages 3.43 yards a carry and gets stuffed on 24.4% of runs, yet the line creates 2.75 yards before contact (8th). Most of the problem is happening after the handoff, not in front of it.

The defense is worse than its rankings suggest. It has allowed 28 points a game to offenses that rank 23rd, 21st, 4th and 20th today, so only one real attack is in that sample. Opponents are completing short, easy passes at will: 0.416 EPA per short pass, last in the league, and an explosive pass rate that is also last. Nothing slows them down. Dallas has 4 sacks, 2 takeaways and a 52.3% third-down conversion rate allowed, so drives keep going and end in the end zone 73% of the time inside the 20. Losing safety Jalon Thompson to IR, with Cobie Durant and DeMarvion Overshown also out, removes three regulars from a unit that had no margin.

The schedule is the reason for optimism. Seven of the remaining twelve opponents rank 21st or worse in offensive EPA, including Philadelphia (29th) twice. That should drag the points-allowed number down from catastrophic to merely bad. The stretch of San Francisco, Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville will decide whether this is a nine-win team or a fringe one. That makes the soft games ahead, starting with a Bucs team on its backup QB, close to must-wins.

strengths.title: Prescott's passing game is elite
strengths.body: Dallas has posted 9.8 or more passing EPA in every game. It ranks 3rd in pass EPA and 4th in success rate while protecting the ball. This is not new: the offense ranked 5th last season, so the efficiency has a track record rather than being a four-game spike.

strengths.title: Pass protection keeps him clean
strengths.body: Only 6 sacks allowed and a 15.5% pressure rate, both top-eight, even though Prescott's time to throw ranks 25th. Guard Tyler Smith is practicing off IR. If he returns, a strength that is already holding up gets reinforcement.

strengths.title: Clean, disciplined football
strengths.body: Two giveaways in four games and the 3rd-fewest line penalties mean the offense rarely beats itself. Ball security in a pass-heavy offense is a quarterback trait more than luck, so it should mostly hold.

concerns.title: Pass defense is broken underneath
concerns.body: Dallas allows the worst short-pass EPA and the highest explosive pass rate in the league. Its deep EPA allowed is a middling 13th, so the damage comes from routine completions turning into big gains, not from getting beaten deep. With a 31st-ranked defense last year too, this is a structural flaw, and the secondary injuries make it worse.

concerns.title: No pass rush, no takeaways
concerns.body: A 3.1% sack rate (29th) and 2 takeaways leave the defense without any drive-ending plays. Combined with a 52.3% third-down rate allowed, opponents rarely face a short field problem. They just keep moving.

concerns.title: Run game stalls after contact
concerns.body: At 3.43 yards a carry with a 25th-ranked stuff rate, the ground game can't close out games, even though the line wins at the point of attack. It hasn't cost much yet because the passing game carries everything, but it limits Dallas's ability to bleed the clock with a lead.

trend.note: The profile hasn't wavered: 20 to 37 points scored and 20 to 34 allowed, and every game went over the total. The only variance is which side made the last stop.

nextGame.headline: Short-week Bucs bring a backup QB and a bad offense
nextGame.body:
Tampa Bay's offense ranks dead last in pass EPA and has allowed 16 sacks on a 10.1% sack rate, and now Baker Mayfield is out with a dislocated thumb, leaving Jalon Daniels under center. That is the best possible opponent for this Dallas defense. The catch is that Dallas's rush can't punish a leaky line, so the Bucs' protection problems may not show up as sacks. Tampa's defense is the real opponent here. It ranks 5th in EPA, 3rd against the run, 6th on third down and 5th in red-zone TD rate. Dallas will have to throw to move it, which suits Prescott anyway.

Availability tilts toward Dallas. The Bucs lose safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (97% snaps) and corner Benjamin Morrison, which weakens a pass defense that ranks a more ordinary 14th. Dallas is without Thompson, Durant and Overshown on defense, but Tyler Smith could return at guard. It is a Thursday game on four days' rest for both teams.

keyMatchups.title: Prescott vs depleted Bucs secondary
keyMatchups.body: Tampa's run defense is elite, so Dallas's 25th-ranked yards-per-carry offense won't move it on the ground. Without Winfield and Morrison, the Bucs' 14th-ranked pass defense is the soft path. Expect a heavy Lamb game plan.

keyMatchups.title: Bucs red-zone defense vs Dallas finishing
keyMatchups.body: Tampa allows touchdowns on only 45.5% of red-zone trips. Field goals instead of touchdowns are how a 9.5-point favorite fails to cover.

keyMatchups.title: Daniels vs Dallas's soft underneath zone
keyMatchups.body: A backup QB in the league's worst passing offense normally means a short, safe game plan. That plays directly into the area Dallas defends worst. Easy short completions could keep Tampa on schedule.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dallas's defense can win early downs against Daniels. If Tampa converts its short throws, a two-score lead never materializes.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is real and should stay top-five. A 2025 history at a similar level, clean protection and low turnovers all support it, though a 30.5-point pace will likely cool toward the high 20s against better defenses like Seattle, the Rams and Jacksonville. The defense should look less catastrophic simply because the schedule softens. Seven remaining opponents rank 21st or worse in offensive EPA. It will still rank bottom-five, because there is no pass rush and no takeaway mechanism to fix it.

With a neutral luck profile, Dallas should land roughly where its efficiency says. That points to a winning record and a real chase of a New York team that is 3-1 and also ranks only 23rd on offense. The division may come down to Week 17 at home against the Giants.
swingFactors: Health of the secondary (Thompson back Nov. 1)
Whether the pass rush produces any takeaways

bets.reason: Dallas is 4-0 to the over, but this matchup is different. Tampa's games average 43 combined points, its defense ranks 5th in EPA and red-zone TD rate, and it is now starting a backup QB in the league's worst passing offense. The Bucs' run defense also takes away Dallas's clock-killing option, which tends to mean field goals rather than touchdowns.

Dallas has won only one of four by more than 4 points. Its 31st-ranked defense makes holding a two-score margin hard, and Tampa's -2.04 wins over expected says the 0-4 record overstates how bad it is. The Mayfield absence is the reason this is a lean and not a stronger play.

confidence.note: Four-game sample, but the offense-up, defense-down profile matches 2025 exactly.
